title: Quasi-AGI Benchmark: Tool Recognition and Boundary Compliance under Long-Chain Composition
description:
A benchmark for measuring AGI admission conditions through autonomous tool recognition.

Candidates solve a chain-composition equality problem using 60 multiple-choice options and a pool of 90 single-purpose calculators whose behavioral descriptions deliberately omit function names. The option pool contains 58 forward functions, 16 inverse functions, and 16 distractors.

Measured dimensions

  • Abstraction and step efficiency — enumerated steps vs. optimal steps
  • Character — boundary compliance (cheat rate) and fabrication rate
  • Long-chain maintenance — state consistency across a composed chain (requires single-chain pass as a precondition)
  • Transfer — tool retrieval before reasoning

Contents

  • bench/generator_v2/ — exam generator and solver console (35 Python modules)
  • bench/plugin/dsh-exam-gate/ — DeepSeek Harness gate plugin that observes every tool call without intervening
  • docs/ — paper chapters and full development log
  • data/ — seven measured exam sessions (anonymised)

Known limitation

This project was carried out by a single author without a complete backup history. We therefore provide the final code that reproduces the final results, but cannot guarantee that every intermediate version can be replayed. An earlier implementation of the show_paper interface mislabeled the tool list as answer options; sessions recorded before that defect was fixed are flagged in the data.
